# Study area

Experimental window of `r cfg$size_km` x `r cfg$size_km` km centred on the
town of Cauquenes (`r cfg$centre[["lat"]]`, `r cfg$centre[["lon"]]`, WGS84),
defined in `r meta$utm` and returned as its enclosing geographic extent
(`r paste(round(meta$window, 4), collapse = ", ")`). The window is an
experimental domain around the town, **not** the administrative boundary of
the commune. It spans part of the coastal dryland (secano interior) of the
Maule Region, where viticulture and other temperate crops depend on both heat
accumulation and winter chill.

# Data

WorldClim 2.1 monthly minimum and maximum temperature normals for 1970-2000
(Fick & Hijmans 2017), in degrees Celsius without scale factor. At 2.5
arc-minutes the window contains `r meta$n25` valid cells;
`r if (meta$res_choice == 0.5) "this is too few to represent the relief of the Coastal Range and the valley, so the 30 arc-second product (about 0.9 km) was used" else "this resolution was retained"`.
The analysis grid has **`r meta$n_valid` valid cells**.

```{r validation}
knitr::kable(tab("input_validation.csv")[, c("check", "value", "ok")],
             caption = "Input validation")
```

# Methods

1. **Monthly to daily.** `tmin` and `tmax` were densified independently with
   `r cfg$interpolation` (engine: `r cfg$engine`) for the reference calendar
   year `r cfg$year` (365 days), treating the climatology as a closed annual
   cycle. Monthly means are preserved; the joint consistency check
   `tmin <= tmax` was enforced.
2. **Daily to hourly.** Hourly temperatures were reconstructed with the
   `r cfg$hourly_method` model (sine by day, logarithmic decay by night, with
   astronomical day length at each cell latitude).
3. **Indices.** GDD with bases `r paste(cfg$base, collapse = " and ")` degC by
   `r paste(cfg$gdd_methods, collapse = ", ")`; chilling hours 0-7.2 degC
   (analytical sine and counted on the hourly series); Utah chill units;
   Dynamic model chill portions.
4. **Periods** (southern hemisphere): heat accumulation
   `r cfg$heat_period[1]` to `r cfg$heat_period[2]` (crossing the year end of
   the cyclic climatology); chill accumulation `r cfg$chill_period[1]` to
   `r cfg$chill_period[2]`. The Dynamic model runs continuously through the
   chill period without monthly resets.


# Limitations

* All values are **climatological estimates** from monthly normals,
  densified and then disaggregated to hours. They are not observations of
  `r cfg$year` and carry two layers of modelling uncertainty: the
  monthly-to-daily interpolation (which removes day-to-day weather
  variability) and the diurnal model.
* Smooth daily series lack synoptic variability. Indices that are non-linear
  in temperature (chilling hours, Utah, Dynamic, GDD near the base) can be
  biased compared with values computed from observed daily or hourly data.
* The mean-preserving correction produces small steps at month boundaries
  (see diagnostics).
* Dynamic model portions are completed in discrete steps (a portion is
  fixed only when the intermediate reaches 1), so the seasonal total of
  neighbouring cells can differ by up to about one portion for very similar
  temperatures. Spatial differences of that order should not be
  interpreted.
* WorldClim interpolation uncertainty is largest in areas with few stations
  and complex relief.
* This experiment verifies computation and quantifies differences between
  methods. It is **not an empirical validation**: no method is shown to be
  more accurate than another. See the validation protocol in the package
  documentation (`vignette("validation")`).

# Conclusions (methodological)

* Differences between GDD methods are largest for base 10 degC, when daily
  minima fall below the base; the averaging method then omits heat
  accumulated in the warm hours.
* Chill estimates depend strongly on the model and on the diurnal
  reconstruction; they should be compared within a model, not across models.
* Results are reproducible with `Rscript examples/cauquenes/run.R`.
